name: tattoo

attributes.attribute: Celtic rite of permanent body marking
dye plant that the Celts used for the body paint

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A tattoo was an old Celtic form of body marking. The word itself came from the South Pacific. The evidence suggests that the Celts also marked their skin for good. The tribal name of the Scoti may have meant the scarred ones. The name of the Picts may have meant the painted or engraved ones. Roman writers said that the Celtic warriors painted their bodies with a blue dye. They used woad, the plant that gave the blue.

okr.objective: Record the tattoo as a Celtic practice of permanent body marking.
key_results: Derives the word from the South Pacific but marks the Celtic custom
States the Pictish name may mean painted or signed ones
States the Celts painted their skin with blue woad dye
